en.title: Isti'adhah and Basmalah
en.body: Al-isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah) is a sunnah when beginning recitation, and its wording is: «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم». The basmalah is recited at the beginning of every surah except Surat at-Tawbah. Between two surahs, the reciter has several permissible ways of reciting.

en.title: Guttural Idhhar (Izhhar Halqi)
en.body: Pronouncing the sakinah nun or tanwin clearly, from its point of articulation, without an audible ghunnah (nasal sound), when it is followed by one of the six guttural letters: hamzah (ء), ha (ه), 'ayn (ع), ha (ح), ghayn (غ), and kha (خ).

en.title: Idgham with Ghunnah
en.body: If, in a separate word, one of the letters of «يَنْمُو» (ya, nun, mim, waw) follows the sakinah nun or tanwin, the nun is merged (idgham) into it while the ghunnah is retained for the duration of two harakahs (counts).

en.title: Idgham without Ghunnah
en.body: If the letter lam or ra follows the sakinah nun or tanwin, the nun is fully merged into it without ghunnah, and this only occurs between two separate words.

en.title: Iqlab
en.body: Converting the sakinah nun or tanwin into a concealed mim when it meets the letter ba, while observing the ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs; it has only one letter, which is ba.

en.title: True Ikhfa (Ikhfa Haqiqi)
en.body: Pronouncing the sakinah nun or tanwin in a manner between idhhar (clear pronunciation) and idgham (merging), free of shaddah (doubling), while the ghunnah is retained for the duration of two harakahs. It has fifteen letters (the letters remaining after those of idhhar, idgham, and iqlab).

en.title: Labial Ikhfa (Ikhfa Shafawi)
en.body: One of the rulings of the sakinah mim: if the letter ba follows it, it must be concealed with a labial concealment (ikhfa shafawi), with ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs. It is called 'labial' because both mim and ba are articulated from the two lips.

en.title: Labial Idgham (Idgham Shafawi)
en.body: If a moving (voweled) mim follows the sakinah mim, the first is merged into the second with ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs, becoming a single doubled (shaddah) mim; this is called 'the minor idgham of two identical letters' (idgham al-mithlayn al-saghir).

en.title: Labial Idhhar (Izhhar Shafawi)
en.body: If any letter other than ba and mim follows the sakinah mim, the mim must be pronounced with a clear labial idhhar, without ghunnah. The greatest care against concealing it must be taken before the letters fa and waw.

en.title: Natural Madd
en.body: The madd (prolongation) without which the letter itself cannot stand, and which does not depend on a hamzah or a sukun; it is prolonged for the duration of two harakahs. The letters of madd are: alif preceded by a fathah, waw preceded by a dammah, and ya preceded by a kasrah.

en.title: Connected Madd (Madd Muttasil)
en.body: That a hamzah comes after a letter of madd within a single word; its ruling is obligatory, and it is prolonged for four or five harakahs whether continuing (wasl) or pausing (waqf), and six when pausing if the hamzah is at the end of the word.

en.title: Separated Madd (Madd Munfasil)
en.body: That a letter of madd comes at the end of a word while the hamzah comes at the beginning of the following word; its ruling is permissibility, and according to Hafs via the route of ash-Shatibiyyah it is prolonged for four or five harakahs.

en.title: Madd for Incidental Stop (Madd 'Arid Lis-Sukun)
en.body: That an incidental sukun follows a letter of madd due to pausing at the end of the word; its ruling is permissibility, and shortening, medium length, or full length are all permitted, though it is preferable to adhere to a single way consistently.

en.title: Substitute Madd (Madd Badal)
en.body: That the hamzah precedes a letter of madd within a single word; its origin is two hamzahs, the second of which was replaced with a letter of madd. Its ruling is permissibility, and according to Hafs it is prolonged for the duration of two harakahs.

en.title: Necessary Madd (Madd Lazim)
en.body: That an original sukun, fixed both when continuing (wasl) and when pausing (waqf), follows a letter of madd; its ruling is obligatory necessity (luzum), and it must be prolonged for six harakahs. It is divided into word-based (kalimi) and letter-based (harfi).

en.title: Qalqalah
en.body: The vibration/bouncing of the letter when it is pronounced sakin (with sukun) so that a strong echoing sound is heard from it. Its letters are five, found in «قُطْبُ جَدٍّ» (qaf, ta, ba, jim, dal). It is minor (sughra) in the middle of a word, and major (kubra) when pausing.

en.title: Rules of the Letter Ra (Heavy and Light Pronunciation)
en.body: The ra is pronounced heavy (mufakhkham) when it has fathah or dammah, or when it is sakin following a fathah or dammah. It is pronounced light (muraqqaq) when it has kasrah, or when it is sakin following an original kasrah that is not followed by a letter of isti'la (elevation).

en.title: Rules of the Lam in the Name of Allah
en.body: The lam of the Name of Allah («الله») is pronounced heavy (mufakhkham) when preceded by a fathah or dammah, and light (muraqqaq) when preceded by a kasrah. This rule is specific to the lam of the Name of Allah alone, not any other lam.

en.title: Tafkhim and Tarqiq (Heavy and Light Pronunciation)
en.body: Tafkhim (heaviness) is a fullness that enters the letter, so that the mouth is filled with its resonance, while tarqiq (lightness) is a leanness in which the mouth is not filled by it. The seven letters of isti'la (elevation), found in «خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ», are always pronounced heavy.
